title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Burgenland and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show the producer, grape, DAC, like Mittelburgenland DAC or Leithaberg DAC, and Reserve for riper wines. Sweet wines show the Prädikat, like TBA or Ausbruch. Austria's red, white and red stripe on the capsule, the Banderole, shows the wine has passed official testing.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Blaufränkisch suits roast duck, goose, venison and goulash, a Hungarian-Austrian dish with paprika. Zweigelt suits Wiener Schnitzel and grilled meat. Sweet wines from Neusiedlersee suit foie gras, blue cheese, strudel and fruit desserts. Serve Blaufränkisch at 16 to 18 degrees.

steps.explanation: Paprika and rich meat suit its spice and acidity.

steps.body: St. Martin's Day, November 11, is when Burgenland celebrates the new wine with roast goose. A perfect match for Blaufränkisch.

steps.prompt: Which foods suit Neusiedlersee sweet wines?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show DAC, Reserve and the Banderole
Sweet wines suit foie gras and strudel
